findings.highlight: Kitahara's going out in his uniform
findings.evidenceJa: だって北原は私服なんだろ？
findings.explanation: Kazusa protests that Haruki gets to perform in ordinary clothes while she has been put in a revealing costume. 私服 is explicitly non-uniform clothing; the English reverses the visual fact and damages the basis of her complaint that the arrangement is unfair.
findings.japanese:
「だって北原は私服なんだろ？
そんなの不公平だ！」
findings.todokanai: "I mean, Kitahara's going out in his uniform, isn't he? It's not fair!"

findings.highlight: Those costumes look so good on you I can hardly resist!
findings.evidenceJa: もう二人とも似合い過ぎててヤバい。どうすりゃいいんだ俺！
findings.explanation: Haruki is overwhelmed and blurts that the outfits suit them so absurdly well that he does not know what to do with himself. “I can hardly resist” invents an object and a sexualized threat of losing control, changing the joke from verbal incoherence to predatory implication.
findings.japanese:
「駄目だこれ…凄ぇ、凄ぇよ…マジスッゲー！
もう二人とも似合い過ぎててヤバい。
どうすりゃいいんだ俺！」
findings.todokanai: "Oh, this is dangerous… Awesome… So awesome… You two look so freakin' awesome! Those costumes look so good on you I can hardly resist!"

findings.highlight: they seem to hate her so much
findings.evidenceJa: 相当嫌ってるらしいからなぁお互い
findings.explanation: Takeya says Kazusa and the music students apparently hate each other. The English makes the hostility one-sided, with the students hating Kazusa, removing her reciprocal antagonism from his explanation of why some have come to watch her fail.
findings.japanese:
「相当嫌ってるらしいからなぁお互い。
笑い者にしたくてしょうがないんじゃないか？」
findings.todokanai: "Then again, they seem to hate her so much. Maybe they're just here hoping to make fun of her?"

findings.highlight: Word has spread even throughout the university
findings.evidenceJa: 大学からもかなり流れてきてたって
findings.explanation: Haruki says that quite a lot of people had flowed over from the neighboring university. The English turns the movement of university students into the spread of information, contradicting the scene's repeated visual accounting of who is entering the high-school grounds.
findings.japanese:
「だからさっきからそう言ってるだろ。
大学からもかなり流れてきてたって」
findings.todokanai: "Just like I said earlier, see? Word has spread even throughout the university."

findings.highlight: I've ever seen her excited even once
findings.evidenceJa: テンション上がってハイになってる冬馬なんてのは、出会って半年の間、お目に掛かったことない
findings.explanation: Haruki says he has never seen Kazusa become visibly amped up or giddy with excitement during the six months he has known her. The English broadens that specific high-energy state into never having seen her excited at all, making her emotional range markedly flatter than the Japanese does.
findings.japanese:
とはいえ、
テンション上がってハイになってる冬馬なんてのは、
出会って半年の間、お目に掛かったことないけどな。
findings.todokanai: That said, it's not like I've ever seen her excited even once in the whole half a year I've known her.

findings.highlight: Even if she makes a careless slip-up now, I'm sure she won't get nervous over it
findings.evidenceJa: 今の雪菜なら、うっかりミスはあっても、緊張で失敗することはあり得ない
findings.explanation: Haruki believes that Setsuna might make an ordinary careless mistake, but she can no longer fail because of stage fright. The English instead says a mistake will not make her nervous, reversing the direction between anxiety and failure and weakening the point of her recovery from the previous day.
findings.japanese:
今の雪菜なら、うっかりミスはあっても、
緊張で失敗することはあり得ないって信じられる。
そんな、強い瞳を俺たちに見せてくれる。
findings.todokanai: Even if she makes a careless slip-up now, I'm sure she won't get nervous over it. I can see her strong determination shining through her eyes.

findings.highlight: even under the dazzling spotlight of the stage
findings.evidenceJa: そんな強い光を受けても
findings.explanation: The “strong light” Kazusa receives is the strength shining in Setsuna's eyes in the immediately preceding narration. Todokanai TL invents a literal stage spotlight, breaking the exchange of looks in which Setsuna's recovered resolve meets Kazusa's calm, fearless expression.
findings.japanese:
で、そんな強い光を受けても、
冬馬の淡々として、それでいて不敵な面構えは、
やっぱり崩れるはずもなかった。
findings.todokanai: And even under the dazzling spotlight of the stage, Touma's detached yet fearless expression shows no sign of breaking for even a second.

findings.highlight: the president, who broke up the club right before the festival
findings.evidenceJa: 同好会を一度は崩壊させた部長
findings.explanation: Kazusa identifies Takeya as the president who once allowed the club to collapse; the last-minute timing belongs to Haruki's subsequent re-formation of it. The English moves “right before the festival” onto Takeya's earlier breakup, inventing a chronology the sentence deliberately assigns to the other culprit.
findings.japanese:
「こんな準備不足で上手く演れるわけがない。
これは全て、同好会を一度は崩壊させた部長と、
時間がないのにやっつけで再結成した北原の責任だ」
findings.todokanai: "There's no way this will end well with our lack of practice. The responsibility is all on the president, who broke up the club right before the festival, and Kitahara who insisted on reforming the club on such short notice."

findings.highlight: if the three of them are this close right now… it's only going to get worse for them
findings.evidenceJa: あんなにどうしようもなくなっちゃったら、これからが辛いよね、あの三人
findings.explanation: Io does not simply say that increasing closeness will make things worse. She sees the three as already having become hopelessly or helplessly entangled and predicts that what lies ahead will be painful. The English normalizes her diagnosis into ordinary intimacy escalating, weakening the scene's explicit foreboding about an unclassifiable bond.
findings.japanese:
「でもさ…
あんなにどうしようもなくなっちゃったら、
これからが辛いよね、あの三人」
findings.todokanai: "But… if the three of them are this close right now… it's only going to get worse for them from now on."

findings.highlight: she half-heartedly accepted because she wanted even more attention
findings.evidenceJa: 本人も軽い気持ちで目立とうと思って
findings.explanation: The imagined audience thinks Setsuna herself chose, on a lighthearted impulse, to stand out. “Half-heartedly accepted” instead makes her a reluctant recipient of the invitation, while “even more attention” invents a comparative degree of vanity. Both the agency and the supposed motive are changed.
findings.japanese:
ただ、人気があるだけで選ばれて、
本人も軽い気持ちで目立とうと思って、
そんな利害の一致しかないと思ってた人も多いはずだ。
findings.todokanai: Most of them probably thought we chose her because of her popularity, and she half-heartedly accepted because she wanted even more attention.

findings.highlight: That's why she can keep watching over us the entire time
findings.evidenceJa: 力加減を必要としない電子楽器は、彼女には物足りないのか、指先を全然見ずに、常に俺たちへと目配りを忘れない
findings.explanation: Haruki speculates that an electronic keyboard, requiring less control of force than a piano, may be insufficiently demanding for Kazusa; she therefore never needs to look at her fingertips and can continually monitor the others. The English reduces this characterizing excess of skill to a generic property of the instrument that simply enables her attention.
findings.japanese:
ピアノの時みたいに力加減を必要としない
電子楽器は、彼女には物足りないのか、
指先を全然見ずに、常に俺たちへと目配りを忘れない。
findings.todokanai: Unlike a piano, an electronic synthesizer doesn't require delicate adjustment of force to play. That's why she can keep watching over us the entire time.

findings.highlight: And the fact they're quiet means that they're earnestly listening to Setsuna's singing as well.
findings.evidenceJa:
というか、皆が聴き入ってるってことはつまり、
雪菜の歌を、もう完全に『聴けるレベル』だって、
認識したってこと。
findings.explanation: Haruki concludes that the audience has fully recognized Setsuna's singing as worth listening to; the English reports only that they are listening earnestly.
findings.japanese:
というか、皆が聴き入ってるってことはつまり、
雪菜の歌を、もう完全に『聴けるレベル』だって、
認識したってこと。
findings.todokanai: And the fact they're quiet means that they're earnestly listening to Setsuna's singing as well.

findings.highlight: I really am the most unreliable member of this band
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が一番心配されてるんだろうな
findings.explanation: Haruki infers from Kazusa's gaze that he is the member everyone is most worried about. The English converts that relational observation into the narrator objectively declaring himself the most unreliable member, changing who makes the judgment and flattening the comic self-awareness of being watched.
findings.japanese:
…やっぱりこのユニットの中では、
俺が一番心配されてるんだろうな。
findings.todokanai: …I really am the most unreliable member of this band of ours, huh?

findings.highlight: In any case, my mind's drifting off to focus on the solo in our second song, but my intuition is still handling this perfectly in spite of myself.
findings.evidenceJa:
何しろ思いはもう２曲目のソロパートに飛んでいってて、
俺のくせに今は流してる感覚が強かったりする。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is already thinking about the second-song solo and feels he is letting the present part flow on autopilot; the English attributes perfect handling to his intuition.
findings.japanese:
何しろ思いはもう２曲目のソロパートに飛んでいってて、
俺のくせに今は流してる感覚が強かったりする。
findings.todokanai: In any case, my mind's drifting off to focus on the solo in our second song, but my intuition is still handling this perfectly in spite of myself.

findings.evidenceJa: 意味ありげな目配せを送る
findings.explanation: Haruki sends Kazusa a meaningful look to cue their rehearsed stunt. A wink is not stated, and “suggestive” adds an English sexual or conspiratorial coloration beyond the functional exchange of glances that the narration repeatedly describes.
findings.japanese:
ずっと俺の手元を注目してた冬馬に、
意味ありげな目配せを送る。
findings.todokanai: I give a suggestive wink to Touma, who's been looking at my fingers all along.

findings.highlight: composed enough to wink back at me
findings.evidenceJa: 俺と目配せで会話できるほど余裕を持っていた
findings.explanation: Kazusa has enough spare capacity while playing a secondary instrument to conduct an actual exchange with Haruki through eye contact. “Wink back” again invents a single gesture and discards the sustained nonverbal conversation used to demonstrate both her technical ease and their coordination.
findings.japanese:
専門じゃないサックスを吹く間でも、
俺と目配せで会話できるほど余裕を持っていた。
findings.todokanai: Despite playing the saxophone, which is not her specialty, she's still composed enough to wink back at me.

findings.explanation: Kazusa's なんだかなぁ expresses dubious exasperation—roughly, she still does not know what to make of this ridiculous success. “I guess, yeah” turns it into mild agreement with Haruki's triumph, reversing the cool resistance maintained throughout their glance exchange.
